oneLiner: Solid-oxide fuel cells sold as time-to-power to AI data centers and utilities that cannot wait for a grid connection or a turbine slot. The market is betting Bloom keeps growing 50%+ into 2027 at mid-30s gross margins; factory capacity and Oracle conversion, not demand, decide whether it does.

verdict.summary: Bloom keeps delivering: a third 2026 guidance raise and operating margins that tripled in a year. But the probability-weighted value sits close to where the stock trades, because the base case already needs FY2027 revenue near $7B and the market still paying ~42x FY2027 non-GAAP EPS at end-2027. The skew is roughly even: the bear case (growth slows to the mid-20s, margins slip on capacity costs) loses more than half, the bull case (Oracle converts, capacity runs ahead) adds about 60%. Two things would move the view: whether the Q3 cash burn reverses in Q4, and whether the FY2027 guide in February clears ~$7B with a firm Oracle tranche beyond 1.2 GW.
wtb: FY2027 revenue of about $7B (+~55% on the ~$4.5B FY2026 guide midpoint), which needs the 2 GW Fremont line running near full by mid-2027.
Non-GAAP gross margin holds at or above ~34% through the capacity ramp and expedited customer timelines.
The Q3 2026 cash outflow is timing: Q4 2026 operating cash flow is positive and FY2026 operating cash flow ends above ~$400M (Q1-Q3: $273M).
Oracle contracts a further tranche beyond the 1.2 GW already firm by mid-2027, so 2028 visibility supports a 40x+ multiple on FY2027 EPS.

bear.why: Capacity or Oracle timing slips and FY2027 grows only ~24%; capacity-ramp costs, pricing pressure from turbines and linear generators push non-GAAP net margin to ~17%. With growth halving the market pays an industrial-growth multiple, not a scarcity premium.

base.why: Fremont's 2 GW line fills, AEP-Google Cheyenne and Oracle's contracted 1.2 GW ship, revenue grows ~55%; non-GAAP net margin ~23%, a little below Q3 2026 as ramp costs offset leverage. FY2028 still looks like 30%+ growth, which keeps a low-40s multiple.

bull.why: Time-to-power stays the binding constraint: Oracle firms a large second tranche, Brookfield-funded projects repeat and capacity steps past 2 GW during 2027, so revenue grows ~90% with ~26% net margin. Multi-year visibility earns a 50x multiple.

scenarioModel.note: FY2026 base ~$4.5B (guide midpoint: Q1 $746M + Q2 $1,065M + Q3 $1,236M + implied Q4 ~$1.45B). EPS = revenue x non-GAAP net margin / ~330M diluted shares: bear $5.6B x 17% = $0.95B = $2.88; base $7.0B x 23% = $1.61B = $4.88; bull $8.5B x 26% = $2.21B = $6.70. Share count is Q3 2026 GAAP diluted 324.3M (which appears to include the if-converted 2028/2029/2030 notes; breakdown unverified) plus ~2% stock-comp creep. Q3 2026 non-GAAP net margin was ~25% (EPS $0.94 x ~325M / $1,236M) vs 20.3% GAAP. Multiples apply to FY2027 non-GAAP EPS at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Can capacity keep 2027 growth above 50% as the base gets bigger?
debates.bull: Demand is not the limit: three guidance raises in 2026, deposits piling up, and the Fremont site can scale toward ~5 GW at ~$100M and 6-9 months per added GW; management is preparing capacity beyond 5 GW.
debates.bear: Year-on-year growth already slowed from +165.5% (Q2 2026) to +138.1% (Q3), Fremont only reaches 2 GW at end-2026, no second factory or timing beyond 2 GW was given, and BTIG flags a near-term margin drag from the ramp.
debates.view: This sets the multiple. Deceleration from triple digits is arithmetic; what matters is whether FY2027 holds 50%+. The February guide is the test, and the base case assumes it does.

signpost.metric: FY2027 revenue guidance and stated 2027 production capacity
signpost.threshold: bullish if revenue guide midpoint >= $7B with >2 GW capacity; bearish if below $6B
signpost.when: Q4 2026 report, ~late Feb 2027 (date not yet announced)

debates.q: Is the profit turning into cash?
debates.bull: Trailing operating cash flow is ~133% of net income, customer deposits and deferred revenue quintupled in nine months, and management says the Q3 outflow reflects working capital for deployments and is not a trend.
debates.bear: The trailing ratio leans on one quarter (Dec 2025 OCF $418M). Q3 2026 OCF was -$27M and FCF -$181M on record profit, with receivables, contract assets and inventory all rising while capex tripled q/q.
debates.view: Plausibly timing for a business shipping 2x the volume, but one more negative quarter would mean growth is being financed on the balance sheet rather than by customers, and the multiple would fall toward the bear case.

signpost.metric: Q4 2026 operating cash flow; FY2026 operating cash flow
signpost.threshold: red flag if Q4 OCF is negative or FY2026 OCF below $300M; confirmed if FY2026 OCF above $400M

debates.q: Does Oracle convert beyond the 1.2 GW already contracted?
debates.bull: The master agreement allows up to 2.8 GW; utilities (AEP's 702 MW Cheyenne plant for Google) and neoclouds (Nebius) show the customer base is widening beyond one hyperscaler.
debates.bear: Oracle is the largest single opportunity and the Q3 call gave no update on reported delays and no formal backlog figure; Jefferies cut its target on exactly that.
debates.view: The base case needs only the contracted 1.2 GW in 2027; the bull case needs a second tranche. Silence through the Q4 call would push probability from bull toward base.

signpost.metric: Firm Oracle capacity beyond 1.2 GW (press release or call disclosure)
signpost.threshold: bullish if >= 0.5 GW added; bearish if Oracle timing is pushed into 2028

thesis: Time-to-power is the product. AEP will build a ~$4B, 702 MW Bloom fuel-cell plant near Cheyenne under a 20-year PPA with Google (announced Oct 14, 2026; fully operational by end-2028), drawn from its up-to-1 GW Bloom agreement, while Nebius's first power block went live in New Jersey (Oct 26, 2026).

The margin step-up looks structural. Gross margin went from 28.1% (FY2024) and 29.3% (FY2025) to a mid-30s non-GAAP level in 2026, which the CFO attributes to pricing, cost-downs and operating leverage, with automation still to come.

Customers are funding the build-out. Deferred revenue and customer deposits reached $754M at Sep 30, 2026 vs $144M at Dec 31, 2025, and third-party capital (Brookfield's $25B framework, Oaktree/IDF's $1.7B for Nebius) lets buyers take power-as-a-service instead of owning the equipment.

Capacity can grow without a new factory. Fremont doubles from 1 GW to 2 GW by end-2026, the site supports up to ~5 GW at ~$100M and 6-9 months per added GW (FY2025 10-K), and management says it is preparing capacity beyond that.
risks: Growth is decelerating off a bigger base. Revenue growth slowed from +165.5% in Q2 2026 to +138.1% in Q3, and the FY2026 guide implies Q4 growth near +90% on Dec 2025's $773M; the multiple follows the second derivative (debate 1).

Cash did not follow profit in Q3. Record net income came with negative operating cash flow and $153.5M of capex, so the strong trailing cash-conversion ratio rests on the Dec 2025 quarter; a second weak quarter changes the earnings-quality read (debate 2).

The dilution headline overstates, but converts still cap per-share upside. Reported diluted shares rose 38% YoY (324.3M vs 234.9M) mainly because the loss-making Q3 2025 excluded dilutive securities; like-for-like non-GAAP diluted shares rose ~3.8% (312.5M to 324.3M). The $2.5B 0% 2030 notes convert at $194.97 (~12.8M shares) and the Nov 2025 exchange issued ~42M shares, so the model uses ~330M.
Oracle has gone quiet. Only 1.2 GW of the up-to-2.8 GW master agreement is firm, the Q3 call gave no formal backlog update, and Jefferies cut its target on the lack of news about delays (debate 3).

Legal, fuel and competitive overhangs. The scandium-sourcing class action (class period Feb 27, 2025-Jul 8, 2026) passed its Sep 28 lead-plaintiff deadline with no appointment found (status unverified); the servers run on natural gas; and AEP bought 190 MW of Mainspring linear generators alongside the Google project, showing a cheaper rival is in the same procurement.
catalysts: End-2026: Fremont 2 GW line complete; any stated 2027 capacity target or second site (debate 1).
~Late Feb 2027: Q4 2026 report - FY2027 guide (debate 1) and Q4 operating cash flow (debate 2).
H1 2027: Oracle tranche announcements under the 2.8 GW master agreement and Project Jupiter deployment pace (debate 3).
2027: AEP Cheyenne 702 MW construction ramp for Google; first funded projects under Brookfield's $25B framework (debate 1).
Ongoing: lead-plaintiff appointment and any motion to dismiss in the scandium securities class action.

points: Revenue $1,235.8M, +138.1% YoY (vs $519.0M); product $1,073.6M (~87%); beat consensus of ~$1.07B.
GAAP operating income $225.4M (vs $7.8M); non-GAAP $285.7M (23.1% margin vs 8.9%); adjusted EBITDA $299.5M.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Oct 22). Revenue of $1,235.8M rose 138.1% and beat consensus by roughly $170M, with product revenue ~87% of the total. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 34.5% and non-GAAP operating margin 23.1%; non-GAAP EPS of $0.94 compared with ~$0.68 expected. The weak spot was cash: operating cash flow swung to -$27.1M as receivables, contract assets and inventory absorbed cash, and capex tripled q/q to $153.5M for production machinery, leaving free cash flow around -$181M. Management called the outflow working capital for customer deployments rather than a trend. Bloom joined the S&P 500 during the quarter. The stock fell ~11% the day after the print, its worst day in three months, as Jefferies (to $242), BTIG (to $250) and JPMorgan (to $292) trimmed targets on Oracle silence, ramp-related margin drag and lower peer multiples, then recovered ~7% on Oct 26.
guidanceProse: FY2026 guidance was raised for the third time: revenue $4.4-4.6B (from $3.9-4.2B in July; ~122% growth at the midpoint), non-GAAP gross margin ~34%, non-GAAP operating income $960M-1,030M (from $800-900M) and non-GAAP EPS $3.10-3.40 (from $2.55-2.85). The range implies Q4 revenue of ~$1.35-1.55B; management said year-end delivery timing decides where it lands. There is no FY2027 guide yet; the CEO said capacity is being prepared beyond the 5 GW Fremont milestone but would not give a date, and expansion will follow orders. Pre-print 2027 consensus was ~$6.8B revenue and ~$4.94 EPS (Oct 12, 2026; post-print figure unverified), close to our base case.
segments: Product: fuel-cell Energy Servers, $1,073.6M in Q3 2026 (~87% of revenue), sold to data centers, utilities and C&I customers, increasingly through third-party financing.
Installation ($84.9M), service ($67.6M) and electricity ($9.8M) in Q3 2026: recurring O&M on the installed base plus power sales; service has historically been the margin laggard.

Options: SOEC electrolyzers on the same platform, carbon-capture-ready systems (the CEO estimates customers would pay a 10-15% premium for zero-carbon power), and 800V DC data-center architecture; negligible revenue today.
competitive: GEV and gas turbines: cheaper per MW at scale, but slots are booked into 2028-29; Bloom sells deployment in months.
Mainspring Energy linear generators: AEP bought 190 MW under an up-to-1.6 GW agreement through 2034 alongside the Google fuel-cell project - the closest like-for-like rival for on-site power.
Reciprocating engines (Caterpillar, Cummins) as bridge power, and over time faster grid interconnection and SMRs compete for the same load.
PLUG and FCEL: subscale and loss-making; Bloom is the only solid-oxide maker at gigawatt scale.
moat: A decade of solid-oxide manufacturing learning gives Bloom the only at-scale SOFC platform, and mid-30s gross margins suggest a real cost-curve lead. There is no patent wall against turbines, engines or linear generators, so the moat is time-to-power plus a bankable delivery record and the financing partners built around it. If turbine capacity and interconnection catch up by 2028-29, the pricing premium erodes.

valPresets.note: TTM FCF is unrepresentative: quarterly operating cash flow has swung from +$418M (Q4 2025) to -$27M (Q3 2026) with working capital and a capacity build, so the DCF anchors on forward non-GAAP EPS (FY26 guide $3.10-3.40). Year-1 growth fades to 3% terminal: bear 8%, base 20%, bull 32%.
